text: In two-stage (dynamic) metabolic engineering, quorum-sensing circuits can be used to automatically switch a culture from a growth-supporting gene expression program to a production-supporting one once cell density crosses a threshold.
explanation: This is true: quorum-sensing switches detect population density via accumulation of a signal molecule such as AHL and flip promoter activity once a density threshold is reached, allowing resources to shift from growth to production automatically without manual intervention. This is a central strategy in dynamic metabolic engineering because exponential growth and product formation otherwise compete for the same cellular resources.
